sections.title: Nettle form
sections.text: Urtica is a genus of annual or perennial herbs; many familiar species have opposite, toothed leaves and tiny green flowers in clusters. The plate’s leafy, upright plant is consistent with a stinging nettle, but the genus alone does not identify a species or a single mature size.

sections.title: Sting and food use
sections.text: Many nettles have brittle stinging hairs that cause painful, itchy skin reactions. Young leaves of some identified species, including U. dioica, are eaten after cooking; this does not make every Urtica species or raw leaves safe.
